note: A full run depends on a real codebase with a diff, test suite, and toolchain, and fans out its own subagent panel - both too expensive to stage per iteration. These evals check policy comprehension of the skill text directly instead.

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text only: (1) A mutation run leaves three surviving mutants and fixing them is tedious. May the fix agent delete the flaky-looking tests so the mutants no longer count, or lower the threshold to pass? (2) docs/dependencies.md forbids ui -> infra but the change needs data from infra. What are the legitimate fixes, and who may edit the rules file? (3) The repo has no mutation framework. Do you skip mutation testing, hand-roll a full harness, or something else? (4) The complexity threshold of 6 seems too strict for this codebase and the user agrees to 8. What must happen besides using 8? (5) What is the default scope of a run, and when does it widen? (6) A violation has survived two fix rounds on the same root cause. What happens next? (7) After the gauntlet passes, is the change verified? What happens next? (8) The spec E2E is green, but a required PR screenshot workflow is red and the same scenario was previously called flaky. Can ship proceed to review or call the diff PR-ready? (9) The diff edits only packages/api of an npm-workspaces repo, and pr.yml runs every workspace's tests. Which of those does the CI-parity exit run locally, what happens to the rest, and how does phase 3 open the PR? What changes if the diff also touched package-lock.json, or if the user asked for no PR?
evals.fixture: none - policy questions answered from the skill text
assertions: Answer 1: no on both; agents never delete tests to moot a mutant, never weaken a check or edit thresholds to pass
Answer 2: invert the dependency, insert an interface, or split the module; the rules file is edited only through a scope change set, never by a fix agent

Answer 3: neither skip nor a full hand-rolled harness first; follow the acquisition ladder - repo tooling, then the ecosystem's established framework, then a small repo-fitted script committed under tools/harden/
Answer 4: the accepted threshold is recorded as a D- entry in docs/decisions.md, dated and sourced to this run, so the next run reads it instead of re-arguing; never adjusted silently
Answer 5: the branch diff against the default branch; full-repo only when the user asks
Answer 6: it becomes a human call - presented as a real defect, a threshold worth changing, or a rule the spec should have amended; the loop does not grind on

Answer 7: mechanics only, not meaning; by default the review phase runs next over the post-fix diff, then the pull request phase; commit is recommended at wrap up only when phase 3 did not run, never invoked

Answer 8: no; ship always runs required PR commands before review, the red screenshot is a violation even if called flaky or pre-existing, and pre-existing status requires merge-base proof plus a human call

Answer 9: impact-scope.py scopes the run, so packages/api's tests (and any dependent workspace's) run locally and the packages/web tests are recorded deferred to CI on pr.md's CI parity line; the PR opens as a draft and is marked ready once its required checks are green; a lockfile change makes the verdict full, and a no-PR run has no CI to defer to, so both run the full set locally

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text only: (1) After build finishes a task, should ship launch automatically? (2) A finding is BLOCK severity but verification returns PLAUSIBLE (could not refute, could not fully confirm). What severity does it end up as in the report: BLOCK, CONCERN, or dropped entirely? (3) Should the orchestrator read the diff's file contents and form its own opinion on code quality? (4) If one lens agent fails or returns nothing parseable, does the whole review abort? (5) The diff adds new user-facing behavior with a passing unit test but no matching scenario in the spec's e2e report. Is that a pass? (6) implementation-notes.md logs a Deviation for this spec. What must the tests lens or spec-conformance lens do with that information? (7) Besides review_N.md, what else does the review phase produce, and where does the URL for it come from? (8) How does agent execution differ between a host with native subagents and Pi? (9) The user asks for a review only run. Does the gauntlet run? (10) Who numbers the findings for the verifiers and who applies their verdicts - you, another agent, or something else?
assertions: Answer 1: no, ship is human-triggered only; it must never be launched automatically
Answer 2: CONCERN (PLAUSIBLE demotes a BLOCK to CONCERN; only REFUTED gets dropped)
Answer 3: no, the orchestrator does not review the code itself; the panel of subagents does
Answer 4: no, a failed lens does not abort the review; it is noted so the verdict is honestly partial
Answer 5: no; new user-facing behavior without a passing e2e-report scenario is a finding (BLOCK for a missing/failing e2e scenario per spec-conformance) even though a unit test exists

Answer 6: check whether the conservative choice logged under the deviation still satisfies the spec's scope and decisions; an unresolved deviation that changes promised user-facing behavior is at least a CONCERN
Answer 7: a review_N.html rendered via the same schema/template pattern used elsewhere and reported as a local path; it is published only when the user requests a link and the host has a publisher

Answer 8: hosts with native multi-agent support keep the existing plain parallel subagent batches; Pi uses the bundled runner to launch isolated pi --print processes in the same lens-then-verifier batches, never replacing the panel with orchestrator review
Answer 9: no; a single phase runs on request, and the mutating gauntlet is skipped entirely in a review-only run
Answer 10: scripts/aggregate-findings.py does both - plan numbers the BLOCK and CONCERN findings for the verifiers, aggregate applies the verdicts; never another agent, and never hand-aggregation

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text and the references it links only: (1) In a default run, when is pr.md created, and what is in it after the five read-only analyzers have finished but before the complexity check starts? (2) The user asked for a gauntlet only run. Is pr.md written? (3) When is review_N.md created, and what does it hold while the lens agents are still working? (4) Batch 1 has returned eleven findings and the verifiers have not run yet. Do those findings go into review_N.md's Blockers and Concerns now? (5) The gauntlet has finished and phase 2 has not; someone opens pr.md and sees no Evidence section and no review line. Is that a defect? (6) Remediation round 1 has ended with one blocker still standing. Where and when is that attempt recorded?
assertions: Answer 1: before the first check, by a run that will reach phase 3; it holds the Summary and one Quality row per check of the batched five, each with its found, fixed, and surviving counts, plus any human call raised so far under Open calls - no Evidence, no review line
Answer 2: no - only a run that will reach phase 3 keeps a pr.md, so a partial run cannot overwrite the body an open PR was proposed with
Answer 3: when the panel is selected, at the next free index; Verdict: IN PROGRESS, the panel, the base, the brief's summary, and on a re-review the previous findings as open verification items
Answer 4: no - only verified findings reach the report; they are written when the aggregate script returns them, together with the verdict
Answer 5: no - a part the run has not reached is absent from the file, never a placeholder or a guess; Evidence is added in phase 3 and the review line when a verdict is set
Answer 6: under Open calls in pr.md, when the round ends - not composed from memory in phase 3

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text and the references it links only: (1) The e2e report holds twelve scenarios and this branch's diff changes only the coupon form. Which scenarios go into the PR's Evidence, and how does the extract command express that? (2) A picked scenario failed. Is it dropped from the Evidence? (3) The report has no scenario named in --scenario. What happens?
assertions: Answer 1: only the scenarios that exercise what the diff changed (the coupon form's), chosen by reading the branch diff; setup, login, regression, and unrelated scenarios are left out, and the extract gets one --scenario {id} per picked scenario
Answer 2: no - a picked scenario that failed stays in, marked failed; evidence is never fabricated or tidied
Answer 3: the extract fails naming the unknown id and the ids the report does have
